implemented.title: The timeout ended before JSON body consumption
implemented.problem: Shared, Feature 1 and chat could receive headers and then wait indefinitely for a stalled body. A fetch-only deadline was not a whole-request deadline.
implemented.change: The common transport consumes JSON inside the request lifecycle. A stalled body reaches the same deadline as a stalled connection.
implemented.validation: Node regressions exercise delayed and unreadable bodies; all 192 Node tests pass.

implemented.title: Cancellation depended on a cooperative operation
implemented.problem: An operation ignoring its AbortSignal could keep its caller waiting; a pre-aborted signal did not prevent work from being started.
implemented.change: Reject pre-aborted work, race the operation against cancellation, deduplicate signal listeners, and remove timers/listeners on every exit.
implemented.validation: Node tests cover pre-abort, timeout, duplicate signals and a non-cooperative operation.

implemented.title: Request/error plumbing was copied across frontends
implemented.problem: Features separately assembled headers, decoded JSON, classified network failures and propagated request IDs. A fix in one client did not reach the others.
implemented.change: Introduce HttpProblem, requestJsonResponse and createJsonClient. Keep feature-owned API paths and compatibility error adapters rather than forcing one domain response envelope.
implemented.validation: Existing feature Node tests still pass; test-only ESM aliases use the real shared source.

implemented.title: Headers and diagnostics could be lost
implemented.problem: Feature wrappers could replace default headers when callers supplied their own. Feature 5 collapsed transport problems into misleading database-unavailable errors or empty successful payloads.
implemented.change: Merge headers case-insensitively, preserve caller request IDs/idempotency keys and retain status/code/cause. Unreadable JSON is an error; 204 is deliberately null.
implemented.validation: Node regression tests exercise header preservation, invalid JSON and the legacy ApiProblem adapter.

implemented.title: Latest-selection logic had no common lifecycle
implemented.problem: A late request could keep running and retain permission to update a screen after selection or navigation changed.
implemented.change: Add createLatestTask, combining actual cancellation with an isCurrent guard. Add cancellable delay and deadline-bounded read-only polling; do not retry writes automatically.
implemented.validation: Node lifecycle tests; full mutation reconciliation is a domain responsibility, not provided by abort.

implemented.title: Market evidence could overwrite a newer selection
implemented.problem: Repeated evidence selection and assistant activity were not consistently invalidated when another case became active.
implemented.change: Cancel old evidence/assistant tasks, pass their signal through transport, and guard state updates. Prevent repeated save/delete actions and keep modal failure feedback visible.
implemented.validation: Existing Feature 2 Node tests plus empty/unavailable mobile dialog smoke. Not full live CRUD.

implemented.title: Due-diligence navigation and question polling could outlive their view
implemented.problem: A detail request or generated-question result could arrive after navigation; polling and map resources had fragmented ownership.
implemented.change: Use separate route/question tasks, bound polling, guard updates, cancel on navigation/pagehide and destroy the prior map controller.
implemented.validation: Node tests and shell smoke; real long-running provider transitions remain a live-stack check.

implemented.title: Buyer case reads, evidence and summaries could race
implemented.problem: Changing buyer cases or refreshing evidence could allow a previous asynchronous result to render against a new selection.
implemented.change: Add view/evidence/summary task ownership. Forward AbortSignal through list, detail, child-list, evidence and summary reads; invalidate older renders.
implemented.validation: Node API cancellation regression plus shell smoke. Child mutation completion is not server rollback.

implemented.title: Repeated initialization leaked listeners and observers
implemented.problem: Drawer rebinding and discarded table regions could retain listeners or ResizeObservers; feature toast timers could dismiss a newer message.
implemented.change: Make drawer ownership idempotent with disposal, add disposeTableRegions, dispose Feature 1 route tables and clear/replace relevant toast/pagehide timers.
implemented.validation: Node tests cover common disposal. Nested Feature 1 re-render disposal still needs an owner-by-owner audit; see D08.

implemented.title: Feature headers were five separate implementations
implemented.problem: Brand styling, product links, search placement and mobile behavior drifted despite existing shared tokens.
implemented.change: Use one shared shell stylesheet and navigation implementation across all five features. Keep local feature routes, filters and business content feature-owned.
implemented.validation: 40 injected-DOM shell cases pass across five features and four viewport widths; normal-origin caveat applies.

implemented.title: Product navigation disappeared or pointed to the wrong origin
implemented.problem: Some feature headers hid global navigation on mobile or used their own product-home rewriting logic.
implemented.change: Keep all four product links visible, centralize integrated/standalone URL resolution and allow an explicit validated deployment home URL. Remove the duplicate Feature 1 link rewriting.
implemented.validation: Node resolver tests; smoke checks all four hrefs and their visibility. Does not click through a real origin.

implemented.title: Fixed header offsets broke wrapping/zoom layouts
implemented.problem: A fixed sidebar top offset could disagree with the actual height of a wrapped product header and workspace strip.
implemented.change: Measure header/strip heights and expose shared CSS custom properties; clean up ResizeObserver on disposal. Add responsive focus/contrast rules.
implemented.validation: Four-width smoke confirms no root overflow in its empty/unavailable fixtures, not every populated/zoomed layout.

implemented.title: Shell consolidation risked adding another CSS override layer
implemented.problem: Leaving obsolete feature topbar/nav selectors in place would preserve hidden cascade conflicts.
implemented.change: Remove 56 superseded header/navigation rule blocks. Keep feature styles only for feature content and use shared semantic tokens for missing colors/focus values.
implemented.validation: Semantic-style gate passes. Reviewed baseline now has 322 entries / 508 occurrences, not zero style debt.

implemented.title: Light-header badges and mobile due-diligence spacing were inconsistent
implemented.problem: Legacy inverse-surface service badges became hard to read on the common light header; mobile layout left excessive blank space and a disproportionately large sidebar.
implemented.change: Use semantic text/status colors for the common header; collapse secondary mobile chrome and anchor the due-diligence content grid at the start.
implemented.validation: Inspected final due-diligence mobile screenshot; mobile empty/unavailable smoke passes.

implemented.title: Initial availability copy overclaimed evidence
implemented.problem: Property and due-diligence headers implied records were available before a request proved it; service health alone cannot establish complete evidence coverage.
implemented.change: Start with neutral research/service wording. Due-diligence readiness reports Review service available, not a claim that all records or evidence are available.
implemented.validation: Product-shell assertions and browser fixtures; no real-data availability claim.

implemented.title: Suburb map failure overflowed the mobile page
implemented.problem: A renderer failure exposed a large raw error/JSON string; the map layout had intrinsic sizing that caused severe horizontal overflow.
implemented.change: Use bounded, user-facing fallback copy, allow the map/grid to shrink, wrap diagnostic text, and prevent generic input sizing from stretching map checkboxes.
implemented.validation: Observed failure in the harness, then reran all eight suburb shell cases with zero root horizontal overflow.

implemented.title: Local static server paths were not contained
implemented.problem: Joining a request path to frontend/shared roots without resolving and checking containment could expose files outside the intended static surface. This server is loopback-only, so this is a local-development exposure, not a demonstrated remote production exploit.
implemented.change: Decode/resolve safely, enforce root containment, reject dotfiles/backslashes/symlink escapes, allow only static suffixes and limit SPA fallback to eligible paths.
implemented.validation: 18 tests cover approved/forbidden paths, symlink escape and proxy route allowlisting.

implemented.title: The development proxy could misframe or truncate requests
implemented.problem: A min(length, limit) read silently truncated large bodies; malformed/negative lengths and unrestricted mutation paths were insufficiently handled. Oversized responses could be silently truncated.
implemented.change: Reject malformed/chunked/oversized bodies, detect short reads, allow only the owned API/explicit health routes, cap responses with overflow detection and preserve HTTP error/request-ID information.
implemented.validation: Source reviewed and syntax-checked; route allowlist tested. Dedicated byte-level proxy integration cases remain required (D11).

implemented.title: WSGI request parsing could read the wrong amount or accept non-object JSON
implemented.problem: Duplicated parsers trusted Content-Length too broadly, including dangerous negative reads, and did not consistently distinguish truncation or JSON shape.
implemented.change: Add a bounded framework-neutral read_json_object helper and use it at Feature 3 backend/database boundaries. Preserve each service's own Problem Details mapping.
implemented.validation: 16 shared parser tests pass, including negative/malformed lengths, oversize, truncation and non-object JSON.

implemented.title: Optimistic concurrency could report a losing update as success
implemented.problem: Feature 3 read an expected version and ran UPDATE ... WHERE version=?, but did not verify that the update affected a row. A concurrent winner could leave the losing request returning current data as though its save succeeded.
implemented.change: Check cursor.rowcount and raise version_conflict when the conditional write loses. Reject bool/non-positive/non-integer versions.
implemented.validation: Repository tests include a competing SQLite writer between the initial read and conditional update.

implemented.title: Month/date strings could look valid without being real dates
implemented.problem: A YYYY-MM-shaped string is not sufficient calendar validation; JavaScript date normalization can turn an invalid due date into another date.
implemented.change: Validate actual calendar months, month order and positive integer versions in saved suburb comparisons; round-trip buyer task ISO dates before accepting them.
implemented.validation: Eight new comparison month/version tests and buyer model Node tests pass.

implemented.title: Tool inputs were interpolated into internal paths before strict validation
implemented.problem: Due-diligence read-only tool endpoints coerced arbitrary input into a review ID, rather than enforcing the exact UUID-object contract declared by their tool catalog.
implemented.change: Require the exact site_review_id object, reject additional fields/non-object values/invalid UUIDs, normalize the UUID, and return an explicit 422 problem.
implemented.validation: 11 pure validator tests pass. Additional Flask endpoint regressions were written but could not run here.

implemented.title: Failed evidence could be presented as no evidence
implemented.problem: Due-diligence code decoded non-200 constraint/building responses and used .get("items", []), silently converting structured upstream failures into empty evidence.
implemented.change: Relay non-200 evidence responses explicitly in deterministic evidence, map and AI-tool paths; only a successful response may be interpreted as an empty collection.
implemented.validation: Endpoint regression tests added for failure propagation; execution blocked by missing Flask/Werkzeug. Pure tool validation is separately tested.

implemented.title: Question generation could conceal a persistence failure
implemented.problem: A generated question pack could be rendered as though safely stored even when persisting it back to the review failed.
implemented.change: Surface a warning that the pack could not be saved and require reconciliation; preserve the generated result without asserting durable success.
implemented.validation: Source inspection and existing frontend tests; authenticated/save-failure browser interaction remains unverified.

implemented.title: Suburb HTML/SVG strings did not consistently escape attributes
implemented.problem: Labels inserted into rendered HTML/SVG could break markup when they contained quotes or untrusted text.
implemented.change: Use the shared text/attribute escaping helper at interpolation boundaries and ignore non-finite numeric chart inputs.
implemented.validation: Node regression exercises the actual trend renderer with a malicious label; this is not a full XSS audit.

implemented.title: A trend line could imply continuity across missing evidence
implemented.problem: Connecting points across a missing month visually implies a continuous observed series that the source does not establish.
implemented.change: Extract a pure trend-path helper that starts a new segment after missing points, while keeping observed zero distinct from missing data.
implemented.validation: Node trend gap, zero and non-finite-value tests pass.

implemented.title: Shared default objects and malformed routes were fragile
implemented.problem: Mutating a returned default checklist could affect future forms; malformed percent-encoding or unknown hashes could interrupt routing.
implemented.change: Clone due-diligence checklist defaults, catch malformed decoding in relevant routers and give suburb unknown routes a deterministic explore fallback.
implemented.validation: Existing/new frontend tests; suburb unknown-route fallback is exercised in the mobile smoke.

implemented.title: Health vocabulary disagreed across feature clients
implemented.problem: A ready service returning healthy could still be labeled partial by a frontend expecting only ready.
implemented.change: Accept the supported ready/healthy readiness forms without claiming that service readiness proves evidence completeness.
implemented.validation: Suburb fixture smoke; no live readiness timing/Compose validation.

implemented.title: Two frontend controllers mixed pure models with orchestration
implemented.problem: Due-diligence and buyer app.js files combined validation/model projection, API clients, rendering, navigation and async orchestration.
implemented.change: Extract Feature 4 models and Feature 5 models/API into feature-owned modules with compatibility exports. Their controllers shrink from 946→816 and 957→731 lines respectively.
implemented.validation: Existing behavior tests retained and updated to inspect/import the extracted implementation; total LOC is not claimed to fall by these controller reductions.

implemented.title: New shared imports were not testable from feature source paths
implemented.problem: Browsers receive copied/mounted shared assets, but Node source tests cannot resolve those deployment-relative imports directly.
implemented.change: Add a narrowly scoped test-only module resolver/bootstrap. It aliases only feature-local shared asset paths; production uses ordinary relative ES modules.
implemented.validation: All 192 Node tests run through the bootstrap; it is not installed in production.

implemented.title: JavaScript syntax checks omitted later slices
implemented.problem: The canonical source-root list covered Shared and Features 1–2, leaving Features 3–5 outside that syntax stage.
implemented.change: Discover every student frontend for syntax checks, while retaining manifest-owned test enablement and excluding vendored sources.
implemented.validation: Canonical compile stage passes; test asserts all five app.js files are included.

implemented.title: The semantic-style gate covered only Shared and Feature 1
implemented.problem: A shared design system is not enforced if later feature styles can add unchecked raw values.
implemented.change: Expand style roots to all five features, reconcile real legacy exceptions and fix the newly surfaced values. The exception ratchet remains explicit rather than pretending legacy debt is gone.
implemented.validation: Style validator passes; baseline entries decrease from 325 to 322, occurrence counts from 517 to 508 despite broader scope.

implemented.title: Default Python discovery/type-check configuration lagged feature enablement
implemented.problem: Root pytest testpaths omitted Features 3–5 and the canonical production mypy list lagged those slices. Note: canonical manifest-discovered feature test commands already existed; this was not a complete absence of feature testing.
implemented.change: Add default testpaths and production type-check targets for later features; align first-party import classification and affected import blocks.
implemented.validation: Selected tests pass on Python 3.13. Full Python 3.12, mypy, Ruff and coverage ratchets remain unverified here.

implemented.title: Shared changes did not consistently trigger dependent feature CI
implemented.problem: Features copied shared browser assets but some path-filtered workflows did not react to shared/frontend changes.
implemented.change: Add Shared frontend triggers to Feature 2/3/4 workflows and use the common Node test bootstrap in feature jobs.
implemented.validation: Workflow YAML parses and consistency tests pass; GitHub-hosted execution was not performed.

implemented.title: CI action/runtime pinning differed by feature
implemented.problem: Integration and some feature workflows pinned actions, while Feature 2/4/5 used moving action tags and relied on a runner-provided Node version.
implemented.change: Reuse the exact checkout/setup-uv/setup-node action SHAs already used by the canonical workflow, pin uv consistently, disable persisted checkout credentials and explicitly install Node. Add bounded runtime/concurrency to Feature 2 and Feature 5.
implemented.validation: Eight workflow consistency tests pass. The pins are aligned to the repository's existing accepted configuration, not independently downloaded/verified here.

implemented.title: Production/development asset projections could diverge after extraction
implemented.problem: Copying a new module into an image is insufficient when a development directory mount hides it. Shared browser, new extracted modules and shared contracts need matching runtime mounts.
implemented.change: Update Feature 2/4 shared browser copies; include Feature 5 API/models/shell assets; ensure all feature shell entrypoints and Feature 3/5 extracted assets plus Feature 3 shared contracts are visible in development.
implemented.validation: Product-shell mount tests, packaging validator and deployment drift check pass; actual image builds/reload checks remain blocked by unavailable Docker.

implemented.title: Shell bootstrapping risked violating CSP or barrel boundaries
implemented.problem: Inlining initialization or importing private shared files would sidestep the existing architecture/CSP contract.
implemented.change: Add tiny feature-owned external shell.js entrypoints importing only browser/index.js. Keep the public barrel free of mounting side effects.
implemented.validation: Product-shell tests assert external entrypoints/public imports for all five features; architecture validator passes.

implemented.title: No small common five-feature visual smoke existed
implemented.problem: The sophisticated retained Shared/Feature 1 UI audit did not itself provide a compact, uniform empty/error shell check for every enabled feature.
implemented.change: Add a separate deterministic Playwright matrix with fixture-only network access, sharding, four widths, empty/unavailable states and selected dialog/drawer interactions. Keep it outside the non-browser canonical gate.
implemented.validation: 40/40 injected-document cases pass, with zero uncaught page errors and zero root horizontal overflow in those cases. Normal browser navigation was blocked before app load.

implemented.title: Shared browser documentation no longer matched actual responsibilities
implemented.problem: Documentation described a Feature 1-centric DOM helper surface, which encouraged more request/navigation duplication.
implemented.change: Document the cross-feature transport/lifecycle/shell contract, cancellation semantics, module loading, cleanup, Node bootstrap and stronger/weaker browser profiles.
implemented.validation: Documentation and public export review; no claim that documentation alone proves runtime correctness.

remaining.title: Production identity and tenant isolation
remaining.observation: Feature 5 uses a configured release0-demo-owner and server-side demo ownership. Internal tokens are service boundaries, not end-user authentication.
remaining.completion_criteria: Agree an identity/authorization contract at the edge and feature APIs; derive the owner from authenticated identity, enforce it on every child/read/write/tool path, and test two users attempting cross-owner access. Keep demo mode explicitly separate. No authentication provider was invented in this patch.

remaining.title: Supported runtime and complete verification
remaining.observation: The full locked Python 3.12 gate, Ruff, mypy, Flask suites, coverage, Docker builds, Compose persistence and normal-origin browser behavior could not run here.
remaining.completion_criteria: Run uv sync --locked --all-packages --all-groups and uv run python scripts/check.py, retain logs, then run normal-origin feature smoke and existing Compose/e2e commands. Fix newly revealed failures before merge; do not lower coverage thresholds to make this patch pass.

remaining.title: Buyer-case pagination can hide records after page one
remaining.observation: The frontend loads buyer cases and child collections with page=1/page_size=100; a sufficiently large workspace can therefore contain records that the UI cannot reach.
remaining.completion_criteria: Implement explicit paging or cursor-based loading using the owned API metadata, with loading/error states and stable ordering. Seed more than 100 cases and more than 100 children; verify every record is reachable and filters do not imply a full-dataset search when they only filter the loaded page.

remaining.title: Large data-platform modules still concentrate too many responsibilities
remaining.observation: The largest unchanged production modules include Feature 1 repository.py (2,568 lines), import_profiles.py (1,794), runner.py (1,348) and release_builders.py (1,347). Size is a navigation/change-risk signal, not by itself a defect.
remaining.completion_criteria: Split by cohesive read/import/publication responsibilities behind existing facade methods. Characterize transaction/lease/publication invariants first; move one concern at a time and run PostgreSQL/PostGIS and ingestion/replay tests. Avoid reworking large stateful code without the database/runtime needed to verify it.

remaining.title: Buyer backend API and shared agent runner remain large
remaining.observation: Feature 5 backend api.py is 1,326 lines and agent-core runner.py is 1,232 lines in the baseline. Both mix multiple orchestration paths with high-cost invariants.
remaining.completion_criteria: Extract pure transition/decision functions and owned route registration modules incrementally. Preserve idempotency, review, durable-run and tool-policy semantics. Run the Hypothesis state-machine suite and persistence/concurrency tests before claiming an architectural simplification is behavior-preserving.

remaining.title: Python HTTP/problem contracts are still inconsistent
remaining.observation: The browser transport is consolidated, but feature Python clients and Problem Details helpers still differ in timeout, error propagation and header handling. Some similar code is legitimate framework adaptation: Feature 3 is WSGI while other slices use Flask.
remaining.completion_criteria: First share a small framework-neutral error/correlation contract and a transport conformance test suite. Extract only demonstrated common behavior. Keep Flask response construction and feature endpoint semantics in their owners; test unavailable, non-JSON, timeout and request-ID propagation at each boundary.

remaining.title: Documented database interpretation disagrees with Feature 4 source
remaining.observation: The living design describes a Feature 1-only PostgreSQL exception while Feature 4 has an actual PostgreSQL-owning store. This review does not infer that a new exception was formally approved.
remaining.completion_criteria: Have the feature/platform owner record the intended exception or migration decision and update the living topology, deployment expectations, backup/restore guidance and assignment evidence consistently. Do not “fix” this by moving credentials into the backend or silently switching database technology.

remaining.title: Lifecycle cleanup is improved, not universally complete
remaining.observation: The new common disposal APIs cover primary routes and controllers. Dynamic Feature 1 subview replacement and all existing pollers/observers still need a lifecycle ownership audit.
remaining.completion_criteria: Instrument active timers, listeners and observers; repeatedly navigate, filter and reopen drawers/tables/maps. Assert counts return to baseline after disposal. Introduce a tiny route-disposal registry only when multiple remaining call sites justify it.

remaining.title: Remaining CSS debt and accessible form/state consistency
remaining.observation: There are still 322 explicit style exceptions, per-feature content rules, different empty/error forms and substantial imperative rendering. The common header does not establish full WCAG conformance.
remaining.completion_criteria: Reduce exceptions by touched area rather than mass restyling. Audit populated states at 200% zoom, keyboard-only focus order, dialog return focus, screen-reader error linkage, forced colors and reduced motion. Add axe/manual assistive-technology checks without treating an automated accessibility score as proof.

remaining.title: No repository-wide checked frontend contract layer
remaining.observation: Plain JavaScript remains appropriate for this project, but domain payload expectations and optional fields can still drift between services and renderers.
remaining.completion_criteria: Add JSDoc/checkJs or targeted generated contract types incrementally to model/API modules first. Keep runtime validation at trust boundaries. Do not start with a TypeScript/framework rewrite that obscures the current behavior and student ownership.

remaining.title: New negative-path tests need the complete execution environment
remaining.observation: The Feature 4 endpoint regressions were written but not executed. The development proxy's framing/response limits were reviewed and syntax-checked, while its automated suite currently targets path containment/allowlisting.
remaining.completion_criteria: Run the Flask endpoint tests with the locked workspace; add socket-level proxy tests for negative/duplicate/chunked lengths, partial bodies, oversized upstream responses, preserved HTTP errors and correlation IDs. Confirm failed evidence never becomes an empty-success result in the real UI.

remaining.title: Dependency/container supply-chain evidence is absent from this review
remaining.observation: Action references now align with existing canonical pinned references. Image tags, dependency vulnerability status and transitive licensing were not independently audited; no CVE-clean claim is made.
remaining.completion_criteria: Run a lock-aware dependency audit and container/SBOM scan in an appropriate environment, review findings against actual runtime exposure, and establish an update cadence. Use digest pinning where reproducibility requires it. Do not mistake actionlint for a security/dependency scan.

remaining.title: Package imports couple pure submodules to application dependencies
remaining.observation: Importing some package submodules eagerly imports the Flask application factory through __init__.py, complicating standalone validation and pure tests.
remaining.completion_criteria: Consider lazy application-factory exports or a neutral core package. Preserve existing public create_app imports and CLI discovery; add import-without-runtime-dependencies and application-factory compatibility tests before changing package initialization.

remaining.title: Operational and business-evidence validation remains separate
remaining.observation: Synthetic empty/error fixtures validate rendering mechanics, not statewide data completeness, evidence accuracy, valuation/statistical methodology, migration safety, backups or provider economics.
remaining.completion_criteria: Keep retained real-stack evidence clearly versioned; test persisted CRUD across restart and failed-dependency recovery. Validate business claims with representative accepted data and feature owners. Run live provider checks only with explicit credentials, budgets and evidence recording.
